Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision at the
intersection in Pasadena, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just give you the facts, but I suppose that's fine. You can note the name on your file.
Q: Understood. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was driving through the intersection on a green light, heading straight across. The light had been green for a little
while, so I wasn't rushing.
Q: What happened next?
A: A pickup came from my right side and went through the red. It hit the passenger side of my car, right around the
middle of the door. There was a loud bang and my car spun partway around before stopping.
Q: Did you have any warinng before the impact?
A: Not really. I saw a flash of white out of the corner of my eye, and then it was over. I didn't have time to brake.
Q: Were you injured?
A: Yes. My neck snapped sideways when we hit, and I've had stiffness and a dull ache ever since. Turning my head
to the left is the worst. I went to urgent care that afternoon and they said it was a strain.
Q: Have you been able to keep up with your normal activities?
A: Mostly, though I've had to take a few days off from lifting and driving longer distances. The pain comes and goes,
and I've been doing the exercises the clinic gave me.
Q: Is there anything else you think I should know?
A: Just that I was following the rules and the other driver wasn't. I'd like this handled quickly.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
</page>
